I tell everyone I know about this app — On April 23, 2025, I downloaded Picnic. It didn’t take long before I decided I needed to have the paid version. I think it was the ability to sort into albums that I actually wanted. It definitely wasn’t “more swipes”, since they’re plenty generous with their number of daily swipes, at least for my purposes. 

I paid for my subscription on May 3. 

Since then, I have missed only 9 days of swiping my “today in years past” on my camera roll. That used to be more of a problem, but then they added a way to be able to do “today in the past” for the past few days. (You get more days of this if you have the paid subscription.) 

On May 23, 2025, I posted online that I had just gotten below 13,000 pictures in my phone roll. 

Today, March 13, 2026, I have 6,248. And during that time I moved into a new house in another country & have taken a *ton* of pictures. So I can’t even say for sure how many I’ve deleted. 

The app does tell you your “sorting status”. I’m not exactly sure how this is measured, as my calculations say I’ve sorted a little over 9 months’ worth of days, but the app says I’ve done 61%.

It also tells you how much space you’ve saved. In just under 10 months (in less than 5 minutes a day), I’ve saved 36GB of space on my phone. I’m hoping that by the time I get through the whole year, I’ll have reduced it by enough to lower my iCloud storage. 

Full disclosure: I did not do the albums after all for a couple different reasons. All I did was swipe left/right & occasionally share an old meme or pic with a friend. 

I’ve tried before to go through my photos & clean them out, but it’s so “steppy”, with having to open each pic to see it, delete, confirm deletion… for 13,000+ pics, it felt hopeless. Plus I had to keep track of what month & year I was on until the next time I could talk myself into trying to make more progress… Picnic does all that. 

Plus, it’s really neat to see all the different things you did on today’s date in the past. I get to relive past vacations & other special events day by day as they happened. And it’s fun to compare, too… a few days ago I came across pics of my Siamese cat from 4 years apart on the same day & got all misty-eyed about how much she had changed. (Siamese get darker as they get older.) 

Tbph, I was planning to get a subscription for a year, organise everything, then do it without the subscription. I was going to put new stuff in albums as I go.

A Horrible Update — So I’ve been using Slidebox for YEARS, even paying for no ads/the ability to sort videos. I really liked the snappy UI, general controls, and organization options, which easily outflanked Apple’s photo app. However, this new update has overhauled an insane amount, making certain features harder and simply removing other features to the point where I’m considering deleting the app all together.

Some annoying, but ultimately forgivable changes include:
- The lack of ability to check your progress with one click(you must save/finish your work so far, and then check)
- The choice to open on a menu to choose where you’d like to start organizing instead of just allowing you to dive right into the action
- The inability to specifically press into a photo to zoom in—this was especially useful for me, as someone with a visual disability

Some debilitating choices, however, include:
- The complete reversal of chronological order—before, I used the “unsorted” option to sort through photos from May, then June, the July and so on, but now not only is there no unsorted option, but the “All” option is most recent-going back. I understand that some may prefer this, but the lack of a choice is infuriating.
- The newfound inability to share photos while I sorted them, which I would do regularly if I found an old photo I cared to share with someone
- The inability to save my progress automatically—I sorted through a few hundred photos, closed the app, and then when I went to reopen they had been unsorted! Apparently, I had to press the X, delete all the photos I had put in the trash, and then I was done, when I used to just be able to close the app at any time and then delete my photos from the trash when I wanted to. The complete change that simply makes it more inconvenient—taking power away from the user in the process—is mind boggling.

I sincerely hope they provide options to return to the classic style of sorting, if the user prefers. Otherwise, I can’t recommend this app.
